scientific.integrity: The theorem is derived directly from the published Adam-mini block-mean second-moment recurrence and its bias corrections. It compares exactly the same silent-history impulse under Adam-mini and coordinatewise Adam, then solves the resulting finite partition minimax problem.
limitations: Silent-history impulse response; pre-existing second-moment mass is not classified.
Only blocks using the scalar block-mean second moment are covered.
The minimax statement concerns worst sparse-coordinate update amplification, not Hessian conditioning or end-to-end training quality.
The later BORA comparison is limited to public abstract and publisher-summary material.

title: Adam-mini has a sharp block-count versus sparse-impulse amplification frontier
